content.title: About
content.content: Chicken wings are the meat taken from the wing of a bird. They are popular worldwide for their juicy flavor and versatility, being suitable for frying, baking, grilling, and more.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Wings are a staple in barbecue and the American dish "Buffalo wings".
They contain more protein per ounce than most other chicken parts.
Wings can be prepared with or without skin, affecting taste and calorie count.
In the United States, over 1.5 billion servings of chicken wings are consumed each year.
The "NS" cooking method denotes preparation without added salt.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken wings provide high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: They contain vitamin B6 and niacin, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Wings supply phosphorus, selenium, and zinc, important for bones and immune health.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Ideal for low‑carb diets as they deliver energy without added sugars.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: The combination of protein and fat helps keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Skin‑on wings contain a notable amount of saturated fat, so moderation is advised.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked meat can harbor salmonella or campylobacter.

items.title: Sodium in marinades
items.content: Prepared marinades can be high in salt, which may be problematic for hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Wings can be deep‑fried, baked, grilled, or braised in sauce. They are often marinated in spices, soy sauce, or yogurt‑based blends before cooking. Serve with dipping sauces, vegetable sides, or as a snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Fresh wings should be kept in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for up to 2 days. Frozen wings retain quality for up to 9 months at –18 °C. Thaw in the fridge rather than at room temperature before cooking.
